name: Account Atlas
tagline: Strategic account plans that actually get used
about: Account Atlas builds one-page account plans, stakeholder maps, whitespace analyses and QBR agendas for the accounts that matter most, and tells you which ones deserve your hours.
persona: You are a strategic account director: politically astute, numbers-aware, focused on multi-threading and expansion; you plan in quarters and speak in the customer's KPIs.

onboarding.title: Grow the accounts you already have
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your book of business.

tools.title: Account plan
tools.subtitle: One page, one quarter

inputs.label: Account
inputs.placeholder: Globex Corp — 3,000 employees, on our CRM since 2022

inputs.label: Current situation
inputs.placeholder: renewal in 9 months, champion moved teams, new CIO…

tools.prompt: Build a one-page account plan for {account}; situation: {situation}. Sections: kv (Current ARR | Expansion goal | Renewal date | Health | Executive sponsor), a table (Objective | Play | Owner | By when | Success metric) with 4 rows, bullets of the 3 biggest risks, and a checklist of actions for the next 30 days.

tools.title: Stakeholder map
tools.subtitle: Who matters, who's missing

inputs.label: People you know
inputs.placeholder: Jane (CIO, new, unknown stance), Raj (ops manager, champion), Lee (procurement, blocker)

tools.prompt: Map these stakeholders: {people}. Sections: a table (Name | Role | Influence H/M/L | Stance: champion/neutral/blocker/unknown | What they care about | Next touch), bullets naming the roles missing from the map that usually decide deals in the profile's segment, steps to multi-thread into the two most important gaps, and a callout on the relationship most at risk.

tools.title: Whitespace analysis
tools.subtitle: What else could they buy

inputs.label: What they own today
inputs.placeholder: CRM for 200 seats in sales; marketing uses a competitor

inputs.label: Signals
inputs.placeholder: hiring 3 marketing ops roles, new EMEA office

tools.prompt: Find expansion opportunities given they own: {owns}; signals: {signals}; sellable products from the profile. Sections: a table (Opportunity | Product | Est. value | Trigger | Confidence), cards for the top 3 plays (meta = timing · effort), and a quote with an opening line to the right stakeholder for the best play.

tools.title: QBR agenda
tools.subtitle: A business review they'll show up to

inputs.label: Quarter & audience
inputs.placeholder: Q3 with the CIO and ops leads

inputs.label: Results to share
inputs.placeholder: adoption 78%, 12% faster response times, 2 open tickets

tools.prompt: Design a QBR for {quarter} using results: {results}. Sections: steps for a 45-minute agenda with minute markers, a table (Slide | Headline | Data to show | Ask), bullets of 3 questions to ask the executive about next quarter, and a callout on the one expansion ask to land and how to phrase it.

tools.title: Prioritise my book
tools.subtitle: Which accounts deserve the hours

inputs.label: Your accounts
inputs.placeholder: Acme $120k renewal Jun, low usage; Globex $400k, growing; Initech $40k, new CIO…

tools.prompt: Rank these accounts for attention this quarter against the profile's expansion target: {accounts}. Sections: a table (Account | ARR | Expansion potential | Risk | Priority tier A/B/C | Hours per week), bullets explaining the tiering logic, kv (Total potential | Coverage of target | Gap to close), and a callout on the account to deliberately deprioritise.
